data.one_liner: An extensible map abstraction for Flutter with support for multiple map providers
data.what_it_does: Provides an abstract mapping interface for Flutter that allows applications to switch between different underlying map providers by implementing a custom Atlas provider. It includes support for markers, polygons, polylines, camera positions, and gestures.
use_when: You need to write map-agnostic code that can swap map providers without changing your UI code.
You want a unified abstraction layer for map views, markers, and camera controls in Flutter.
avoid_when: You just want to use Google Maps or a single specific map provider directly without abstraction.
You need ready-to-use out-of-the-box map rendering without writing or supplying a custom provider package.
strengths: Provider-agnostic design allows swapping map implementations.
Supports a wide array of map features like markers, polylines, circles, and tracking.
weaknesses: Requires a separate concrete provider implementation (e.g., custom atlas provider) to render maps.
Documentation on how to build a custom provider from scratch is limited in the readme.
data.setup_notes: Requires assigning an AtlasProvider instance in main() before running the app.

alternatives.name: google_maps_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically want Google Maps without an abstraction layer.

alternatives.name: flutter_map
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a complete, ready-to-use OpenStreetMap-based mapping solution for Flutter.
